title: Impaired Consciousness, Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS), and Multiorgan Dysfunction Syndrome (MODS) As the Triad of Mortality in Severe Dengue: Evidence From 100 Consecutive ICU Admissions

analysis.research_question_and_background: Severe dengue is a leading contributor to intensive care unit (ICU) admissions and death in tropical regions, and identifying factors associated with poor outcomes early is critical for guiding treatment and allocating resources in critically ill patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective observational cohort enrolled 100 consecutive patients with WHO 2009-defined severe dengue admitted to the ICU and Emergency Department of Maharishi Markandeshwar Institute of Medical Science and Research (MMIMSR), Mullana, Haryana, between March 2025 and January 2026.
analysis.methods: Clinical, laboratory, and severity-score data (Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II), Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA)) were recorded and compared between survivors and non-survivors using appropriate statistical tests, relative risks (RR) with 95% CI, and ROC analysis.
analysis.main_results: ICU mortality was 21.0% (21/100), and thrombocytopenia showed no mortality link (p = 0.678). Impaired consciousness (RR 103.20), acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS; RR 7.55), and multiorgan dysfunction syndrome (MODS; RR 6.08) showed the strongest associations with mortality, while APACHE II (AUC 0.935) and SOFA (AUC 0.938) had the best discriminative accuracy.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Impaired consciousness, ARDS, and MODS strongly predicted mortality in this severe dengue cohort, forming a clinically vital cluster for early risk stratification, and these single-center findings question the thrombocytopenia-centric paradigm.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support closer attention to neurological status and organ dysfunction from ICU admission onward to guide treatment and resource allocation in critically ill patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the single-center design and limited sample size of 100 consecutive patients, which may affect generalisability.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective observational cohort study analyzed 100 consecutive patients with severe dengue admitted to an ICU in India between March 2025 and January 2026 to identify factors associated with mortality. The overall ICU mortality rate was 21.0%, and thrombocytopenia was not linked to mortality. The study found that impaired consciousness, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and multiorgan dysfunction syndrome (MODS) were the strongest predictors of death, with APACHE II and SOFA scores demonstrating high discriminative accuracy. These results challenge the thrombocytopenia-centric paradigm and suggest that early risk stratification should focus on neurological status and organ dysfunction. The single-center design indicates moderate evidence strength.

title: A hierarchical clock-mixture model for Bayesian phylogenetic dating

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the problem of conditioning Bayesian phylogenetic time tree inference on a single molecular clock model, which treats clock choice as fixed even when support among plausible clock families is uncertain, potentially distorting estimated timescales and their uncertainty.

analysis.main_results: In stratified simulations, the generating clock family was retained in the 95% posterior model set in all replicates, and model-averaged estimates of the overall substitution rate, root age, and tree length remained accurate; on a DENV-4 benchmark, the mixture reproduced the higher-effort nested-sampling ranking of clock families while avoiding extreme run-to-run variability.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that clock-model support and downstream timescale sensitivity are related but not identical, and that single-clock dating analyses can still be adequate, but fixing a clock model should be justified by posterior support rather than treated as a default assumption.

title: Evaluating Elevated D-Dimer Levels Associated Clinical Conditions in Hospitalised Patients: A Cross-sectional Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Elevated plasma D-dimer levels are not specific to thromboembolic disorders and may be observed in several non-thrombotic conditions, complicating interpretation in resource-limited rural settings.
